long_description:
Regard is a clinical AI platform that functions as an automated co-pilot for hospitalists and inpatient physicians. The system continuously analyzes patient charts in real-time, identifying conditions that may be missed during documentation and surfacing evidence-based diagnostic recommendations directly within the clinical workflow.

The platform excels at condition capture and clinical decision support in the inpatient setting. Regard's AI engine reviews labs, vitals, medications, and clinical notes to identify patterns suggesting undiagnosed conditions, helping improve diagnostic accuracy and clinical documentation integrity. The company reports that physicians accept approximately 70% of the diagnoses Regard recommends.

With over 150 hospitals using the platform and more than 9 million diagnoses recommended, Regard has established itself as a leader in hospital-focused clinical AI. The company raised $61 million in Series B funding at a $350 million valuation and has partnered with Microsoft to integrate with Dragon Copilot, the leading ambient AI scribe in enterprise healthcare.

Regard integrates natively with Epic and is designed specifically for inpatient settings. The platform is not intended for ambulatory care, therapy notes, or mental health documentation—it focuses squarely on medical diagnosis capture and clinical decision support for hospital medicine.

faqs.a: Regard is a clinical AI co-pilot that automatically reviews patient charts in hospitals to identify missed diagnoses and conditions. It surfaces evidence-based recommendations to hospitalists, improving diagnosis capture and documentation quality.

Regard is not an ambient AI scribe—it doesn't transcribe conversations or generate clinical notes. It's a diagnostic support tool that analyzes existing chart data to identify conditions that may need documentation or treatment.
Regard integrates natively with Epic. The company has also partnered with Microsoft to integrate with Dragon Copilot for ambient documentation capabilities.
Regard reports that physicians accept approximately 70% of the diagnoses it recommends. The platform has recommended over 9 million diagnoses across 150+ hospitals.
